edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Εἰ δ᾿ ἀκριβῶς χρὴ ἡμᾶς λέγειν τὰ πρὸς τὸν Κέλσον, οἰόμενον τὰ αὐτὰ ἡμᾶς Ἰουδαίοις περὶ τῶν ἐκκειμένων δοξάζειν, φήσομεν ὅτι τὰ μὲν βιβλία θείῳ γεγράφθαι πνεύματι ὁμολογοῦμεν ἀμφότεροι, περὶ δὲ τῆς ἐκδοχῆς τῶν ἐν τοῖς βιβλίοις οὐκέτι τὰ ὅμοιά φαμεν, οἵ γε οὐδὲ βιοῦμεν ὡς Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ φρονεῖν οὐ τὴν κατὰ τὸ ῥητὸν ἐκδοχὴν τῶν νόμων εἶναι τὴν περιέχουσαν τὸ βούλημα τῆς νομοθεσίας. καὶ λέγομεν δ᾿ ὅτι, „ἡνίκα ἂν ἀναγινώσκηται Μωϋσῆς, κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν κεῖται“ τῷ τοῖς τὴν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μὴ ἀσπασαμένοις ὁδὸν ἐπικεκρύφθαι τὸ βούλημα τοῦ Μωϋσέως νόμου. ἴσμεν δ᾿ ὅτι, „ἐὰν ἐπιστρέψῃ τις πρὸς τὸν κύριον“ („ὁ δὲ κύριος τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστι“), περιαιρεθεὶς „τὸ κάλυμμα“ „ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν“ ἐν τοῖς κεκρυμμένοις νοήμασι κατὰ τὰ γράμματα „δόξαν τοῦ κυρίου“ ὡσπερεὶ κατοπτρίζεται καὶ μεταλαμβάνει τῆς καλουμένης θείας δόξης εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ δόξαν (τροπικῶς μὲν λεγομένου προσώπου γυμνότερον δ᾿, ὡς ἂν ὀνομάσαι τις, τοῦ νοῦ). ἐν ᾧ ἐστι τὸ [τοῦ] „κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον“ πρόσωπον, πληρούμενον φωτὸς καὶ δόξης ἀπὸ τῆς περὶ τῶν κατὰ τοὺς νόμους ἀληθείας.
thought_title: The veil over the reading of Moses
pass_a_gloss: If we must say precisely the [replies] toward Celsus, who thinks we hold the same as Jews about the matters set out, we shall say that we both confess the books to have been written by divine Spirit, but about the interpretation of the things in the books we no longer say similar things; we who do not even live as Jews, by thinking that not the interpretation according to the letter of the laws is the one containing the intention of the legislation. And we say that 'whenever Moses is read, a veil lies on the heart' [2 Cor 3:15] by the intention of the law of Moses having been hidden from those not having embraced the way through Jesus Christ. And we know that 'if one turns to the Lord' [2 Cor 3:16] ('and the Lord is the Spirit' [2 Cor 3:17]), having had removed 'the veil', 'with unveiled face' he as it were mirrors/beholds 'the glory of the Lord' [2 Cor 3:18] in the thoughts hidden according to the letters, and partakes of the so-called divine glory unto his own glory (face being said figuratively, but more barely, as one might name it, the mind ). In which is the face 'according to the inner man' [Rom 7:22], being filled with light and glory from the truth concerning the things in the laws.

pass_b_english: If we must answer Celsus precisely, since he thinks that we hold the same opinions as the Jews on the matters set out, we will say this. We both agree that the books were written by the divine Spirit; but about the interpretation of what is in the books we no longer say the same things. We do not even live as the Jews do, because we judge that the literal interpretation of the laws is not the one that contains the intention of the legislation.

And we say that “whenever Moses is read, a veil lies upon the heart” (2 Corinthians 3:15), because the intention of the law of Moses has been hidden from those who have not embraced the way that comes through Jesus Christ. But we know that “if anyone turns to the Lord” (and “the Lord is the Spirit”) (2 Corinthians 3:16–17), then, with “the veil” taken away, he beholds as in a mirror, “with unveiled face,” “the glory of the Lord” (2 Corinthians 3:18) that lies in the thoughts hidden beneath the letter, and receives a share of what is called the divine glory, for his own glory. Here “face” is said figuratively; to name it more plainly, as one might, it is the mind. In the mind is the face of the “inner man” (Romans 7:22), filled with light and glory from the truth about what is in the laws.
notes: Origen speaks throughout; no Celsus quotation here. 'θείῳ πνεύματι' = the Holy Spirit, capitalized. 2 Corinthians 3:15 is quoted nearly word for word (Paul has 'their heart'; Origen omits αὐτῶν). 3:16-18 are quoted in pieces and recast: Origen makes 'the glory of the Lord' the glory 'in the hidden meanings of the letters', and 'εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ δόξαν' adapts Paul's 'from glory to glory' (3:18); rendered 'to become his own glory'. The parenthesis 'τροπικῶς μὲν λεγομένου προσώπου γυμνότερον δ᾿... τοῦ νοῦ' (face = mind) is given as its own sentence. 'κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον' quotes the exact phrase of Romans 7:22 (compare 2 Corinthians 4:16, Ephesians 3:16); the bracketed [τοῦ] of the edition is ignored. The relative 'ἐν ᾧ' is taken to refer to the mind (νοῦς).
Pass A: the inline Greek lemma tags were moved out of the gloss into lemmas[] (the gloss was over a quarter Greek); the English gloss is unchanged.
